failure_summary.description: New hotel-star or neighborhood constraints were not applied to suitable cached results; agents returned no plan, only retrieved results, or reran proximity search.
Agents omitted required cache saves, duplicated result-producing calls, or used unsupported date calculations.
An attraction search omitted its required city or state and treated a suggested area as a named-attraction search.
A flight filter used an invalid time format.

patch.reasoning: Most observed failures concern rules the skill already states explicitly, so repeating tool-persistence, time-format, or neighborhood-update guidance is unlikely to help. Two useful gaps remain: explicitly distinguish hotel star criteria from review ratings, and state the attraction location requirement while clarifying how to filter a suggested area versus search for a named attraction.

edits.target: For ratings, treat a single numeric rating without minimum or “at least” language as exact `[x, x]`; “exactly x” is `[x, x]`, and an explicit “at least x” request is `[x, 5]`.
edits.content: For hotel star criteria, use the `stars` field rather than review `rating`: “at least x stars” maps to `[x, 5]`, and an exact x-star request maps to `[x, x]`.

`search_attractions` requires at least one of `city` or `state`, even though both fields are individually optional in the schema; reuse an established location or seek it if absent. For follow-ups about an assistant-suggested place, distinguish an area from a named attraction: filter cached attraction results by `neighborhood` for an area, and use `attraction_name` when the user requests the named attraction itself.
